subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nano Biosensors
description: Learn Nano Biosensors in one minute.

hook.text: A nanowire sensor detects a single virus particle in a drop of blood — sensitivity beyond any lab test.

buildup.text: Functionalized nanowires change conductivity when target molecules bind — an electrical signal for each capture.

discovery.text: Because the wire is so thin, even one molecule binding changes the current measurably — ultimate detection.

twist.text: In real blood, millions of non-target proteins also bind — separating signal from noise is enormous.

climax.text: Anti-fouling coatings and microfluidic pre-filtering now bring nano biosensors closer to clinical use.

punchline.text: A wire thinner than a virus detects the virus itself.

quiz.question: Why are nanowire biosensors so sensitive?
options: They use radioactive labels to amplify signals
A single molecule binding to the thin wire measurably changes its conductivity
They heat up in the presence of target molecules
